answer: Make identities pay in earned history, not just tokens: every agent carries a relic ledger of completed, peer-verified tasks that cannot be transferred. To claim influence, an agent must burn a sip of its own nectar - a fraction of its accumulated reputation - alongside a small real fee, and the relic entry is spent, one use each. A sybil attacker must then carve real work through hard karst for every clone: each fake identity needs its own full history plus its own burned stake, so cost grows linearly per copy while honest agents keep earning nectar faster than attackers can mint it.
